【P1｜Mr. Utterson】
别称：G. J. Utterson、Gabriel John Utterson、Utterson
当前一句话身份：Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
档案（最新）：occupation：lawyer；personality：uneasy and concerned for Jekyll；situation：last good influence on downgoing men；residence：bachelor house near a church；identity：lawyer
关系：Mr. Richard Enfield（cousin）、Dr. Jekyll（client and friend whose affairs he handles）、Dr. Lanyon（friend who left him a narrative）、Sir Danvers Carew（lawyer who identifies him）、Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard（police officer assisting him）、Mr. Guest（employee）、Bradshaw（subordinate）、Poole（butler of Jekyll who assists him）、the man in the middle（beneficiary named in Jekyll's earlier will）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Utterson greets Jekyll and hopes he is better.
- Utterson introduces his cousin Mr. Enfield to Dr. Jekyll and invites Jekyll out.
- Utterson proposes they stay below and talk from where they are.
- The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror.
- Utterson says 'God forgive us' twice.
- Poole comes to Utterson's house at night and says something is wrong.
- Poole says the doctor has shut himself in the cabinet and he is afraid.
- Poole says he thinks there has been foul play.
- Utterson rises, takes hat and greatcoat, and follows Poole.
- They walk through the cold deserted London streets to the house.
- They enter the hall where all the servants are huddled in fear.
- The housemaid whimpers and the maid weeps loudly.
- Poole leads Utterson to the laboratory and tells him to listen quietly.
- Poole asks whether that was his master's voice; Utterson says it seems much changed.
- Utterson calls the tale wild and argues a murderer would not stay.
- Poole hands Utterson a crumpled note from Dr. Jekyll to Messrs. Maw.
- Utterson notes the handwriting is the doctor's; Poole says he has seen him.
- Poole tells Utterson he saw a masked figure in the cabinet.
- Utterson suggests Jekyll suffers a deforming disease and hides his face.
- Poole insists the masked thing was not Jekyll but a dwarf.
- Utterson resolves to break in the cabinet door.
- Poole and Utterson agree to break in together.
- Poole fetches an axe and suggests Utterson take the kitchen poker.
- Utterson warns Poole they are placing themselves in peril.
- Poole says the masked figure was Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson says he once spoke with Hyde.
- Poole describes Hyde as giving a cold, thin feeling.
- Utterson summons Bradshaw and orders him to guard the laboratory door.
- Poole and Utterson wait in the theatre and hear pacing footsteps.
- Poole says the walker weeps like a woman or lost soul.
- Utterson demands to see Jekyll and threatens brute force.
- The voice begs Utterson for mercy.
- Utterson recognizes the voice as Hyde's and orders the door down.
- They peer in and find the contorted body of Edward Hyde.
- Utterson concludes Hyde is a self-destroyer by the crushed phial.
- Utterson says they must now find Jekyll's body.
- Utterson and Poole search the theatre, cabinet, closets and cellar for Jekyll.
- They find the by-street door locked with a rusty broken key lying nearby.
- They examine the cabinet and find chemical apparatus and white salt on saucers.
- They find a pious book annotated by Jekyll with startling blasphemies.
- They look into the cheval-glass and see only the room and their own pale faces.
- Utterson opens an envelope addressed to him and finds a will naming himself instead of Hyde.
- Utterson reads Jekyll's dated note and concludes Jekyll was alive that day and may have fled.
- Poole hands Utterson a sealed packet, the third enclosure.
- Utterson decides to go home, read the documents, and return before midnight to send for the police.

【P7｜Dr. Jekyll】
别称：Dr. Henry Jekyll、Dr. J.、HENRY JEKYLL、Harry、Harry Jekyll、Henry Jekyll
当前一句话身份：Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
档案（最新）：identity：doctor and owner of the house；situation：said to have been made away with eight days ago；age：fifty；appearance：tall, fine build of a man；personality：known for charities and religion；residence：house with laboratory and cabinet
关系：Mr. Utterson（lawyer and friend）、the man in the middle（patron of Hyde）、Dr. Lanyon（old friend now estranged）、Poole（servant）、Mr. Richard Enfield（acquaintance）
至今经历（按时间）：
- The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.
- Utterson asks whether he and Lanyon are Jekyll's two oldest friends.
- Lanyon says Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago.
- Utterson stays behind after Jekyll's dinner to speak with him.
- Utterson raises the subject of Jekyll's will.
- Jekyll calls Lanyon a hide-bound pedant and says he was disappointed in him.
- Utterson says he has learned something of young Hyde.
- Jekyll pales and refuses to hear more about Hyde.
- Utterson offers to help Jekyll out of the matter in confidence.
- Jekyll says he can be rid of Mr. Hyde whenever he chooses.
- Jekyll says he takes a great interest in poor Hyde.
- Jekyll asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when he is gone.
- Utterson promises to bear with Hyde and get his rights for him.
- Utterson recognizes the stick as one he gave Henry Jekyll.
- Utterson is admitted by Poole and received into Jekyll's cabinet.
- Jekyll swears he will never set eyes on Hyde again.
- Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde to judge.
- Jekyll says he burned the envelope and it bore no postmark.
- Jekyll admits Hyde dictated the terms of his will.
- Jekyll emerges from seclusion and resumes his old friendships.
- Utterson dines with Jekyll and Lanyon as inseparable friends.
- Jekyll shuts his door against Utterson, Poole reporting he is confined.
- Utterson writes to Jekyll, who replies of an incurable quarrel.
- Jekyll vows extreme seclusion and speaks of an unnameable punishment.
- The enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance.
- Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.
- Utterson sees Dr. Jekyll sitting sadly at the middle window.
- Utterson greets Jekyll and hopes he is better.
- Jekyll replies he is very low and says it will not last long.
- Utterson introduces his cousin Mr. Enfield to Dr. Jekyll and invites Jekyll out.
- Jekyll declines the walk, saying it is quite impossible and he dare not.
- Utterson proposes they stay below and talk from where they are.
- Jekyll's smile turns to abject terror and the window is thrust down.

【P2｜Mr. Richard Enfield】
别称：Enfield、Mr. Enfield、Richard
当前一句话身份：Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
档案（最新）：identity：Utterson's distant kinsman；personality：dislikes asking questions, calls it delicacy；situation：studied the door place himself
关系：Mr. Utterson（cousin）、Dr. Jekyll（acquaintance）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Enfield points his cane at a sinister door and asks Utterson if he ever remarked it.
- Enfield says the door is connected with a very odd story.
- Enfield collars the man and brings him back to the group around the child.
- They threaten scandal and force the man to pay a hundred pounds.
- The man offers to stay until the banks open and cash the cheque himself.
- They spend the night in Enfield's chambers and go to the bank next day.
- Enfield presents the cheque believing it a forgery, but it proves genuine.
- Enfield calls the door place Black Mail House and muses.
- Enfield explains his rule of not asking questions.
- Enfield describes the door house: no other door, clean shut windows, smoking chimney.
- Utterson asks the name of the man who walked over the child.
- Enfield names the man as Hyde.
- Enfield describes Hyde as deformed and detestable.
- Utterson says he already knows the other party's name.
- Enfield confirms Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago.
- Enfield and Utterson agree never to refer to the matter again.
- Utterson and Enfield stop before the by-street door on their Sunday walk.
- Enfield says the Hyde story is at an end and they will never see Hyde again.
- Enfield reveals he learned the door was a back way to Dr. Jekyll's.
- They enter the court to look at the windows, Utterson uneasy about Jekyll.
- Utterson introduces his cousin Mr. Enfield to Dr. Jekyll and invites Jekyll out.
- The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror.

[note_g1]
Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield。Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

[note_g2]
Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house。Poole is the elderly butler of Dr. Jekyll's house and the servant who directs the search after the cabinet is broken open. He is frightened and worn, with a white face and a harsh broken voice, and for about a week he has been unable to bear the situation. He long served Jekyll, admitted Utterson to the cabinet, and reported that Jekyll confined himself over the laboratory. When he came to Utterson's house at night, he said the doctor had shut himself in and he feared foul play. He led Utterson to the laboratory, told of the masked figure, and struck the door with an axe. He now hands Utterson the sealed packet and awaits the police.

[note_g3]
Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir。Dr. Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, owner of the house with laboratory and cabinet, and the friend and client of Mr. Utterson. He is tall and well built, known for charities and religion, but has become fanciful and estranged from Dr. Lanyon. His will left all his possessions to Edward Hyde, and he admitted Hyde dictated its terms. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, then resumed his old friendships before shutting his door against Utterson and vowing extreme seclusion. He was last seen sitting sadly at the middle window, declining to walk out. He is said to have been made away with eight days ago, and his body has not been found.

[note_g4]
Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town。Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

[note_g5]
Voice inside the cabinet refusing entry。The voice is the unseen speaker inside Dr. Jekyll's cabinet, heard by Poole and Mr. Utterson during the night search. It complains that it cannot see anyone and begs Utterson for mercy. It is connected to Poole only as the servant who knocks and calls through the door. After Poole reports that the doctor has shut himself in, the voice answers from within and refuses entry. Utterson recognizes it as Hyde's voice and orders the door down. The voice is now silent, its speaker found dead inside the cabinet.

[note_g6]
Servant who weeps hysterically。The housemaid is a servant in Dr. Jekyll's house, subordinate to Poole and a colleague of the cook. She is hysterical and weeping. When Poole led Utterson into the hall, all the servants were huddled in fear, and she whimpered while the maid wept loudly. She remains in the hall with the other frightened servants as Utterson and Poole proceed to the laboratory.
